issues.description: Method addGuestStudents: The template declares addGuestStudents with signature addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) (template src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java), but the problem statement/UML and the solution declare addGuestStudents(int) without a boolean parameter (problem_statement.md and solution src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java). This parameter mismatch forces students to either modify the provided signature (which they may avoid) or implement the wrong signature compared to the specification and solution, causing compilation/test mismatches and confusion about the intended API.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the template method signature to match the problem statement and solution: declare public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { /* TODO: implement and optionally validate input internally */ } Remove the additional boolean parameter from the template. If input validation is desired for teaching purposes, implement the validation inside the single-parameter method or provide an overloaded private helper, but keep the public API identical to the specification.

issues.description: The concept is the method for adding guest students to a Lecture. The problem statement specifies a method named addGuestStudents with a single int parameter: addGuestStudents(int). The solution implementation provides public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents). However, the template stub declares public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents, boolean validateInput) — i.e., it adds an extra boolean parameter. This discrepancy between the template signature and both the problem description and the solution makes it unclear which method students should implement (single-parameter vs two-parameter) and whether they must provide validation logic via a parameter. Students may be blocked or confused when their implementation does not match the expected single-parameter signature used by tests and the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub to match the problem statement and solution: replace the two-parameter signature with the single-parameter method used in the task and solution: public void addGuestStudents(int numberOfNewGuestStudents) { ... }. If input validation is desired, implement it inside this method or provide a clearly-documented helper method, but keep the public API signature identical to the specification to avoid confusing students and breaking automated tests.
